structural_cause.one_line: A non-zero wrapper exit under `set -e` aborted the step AT the wrapper line, so the log was never tailed and never uploaded -- the failure was structurally silent on every carrier.
structural_cause.detail: ssm.tf line 49 ran `set -e`; line 65 ran `./run-bd-auto-login.sh > $LOG_FILE 2>&1` bare. Under set -e a non-zero exit terminates the shell immediately, so lines 66-69 (`EXIT_CODE=$?`, `tail -25`, `aws s3 cp`, `exit $EXIT_CODE`) were UNREACHABLE on the failure branch. `EXIT_CODE=$?` was dead code. The document still reported Failed with rc 1, which is why the failure was visible as a status and invisible as a reason.
structural_cause.deployed_bytes_confirmed_not_drift: aws ssm get-document --name opal-cot-bd-session-fetch (876 bytes) was byte-identical to repo HEAD on this step before the change, so the deployed bytes carried the same dead code -- this was a defect in the build input, not drift away from it.

why_it_stayed_broken_4_days.text: Nothing retried and nothing surfaced. The cot box carries no in-run login retry: /opt/bd-cot-auto-login/secret-ids.env (1200 bytes, md5 9b55e03c9575d4f6b58d1d239c8409fb) does NOT set BD_MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS or BD_LOGIN_BACKOFF_MS, while the repo copy (1660 bytes, md5 3c4298378faa5811b7e0eaf7a192ca2c) does and marks them 'Inert until the new .js is box-deployed (CTO-gated)'. So one transient login failure = one lost day, four times over, with no log to read. NOT REMEDIATED HERE: the retry needs the newer .js, which is not in this order's grant.

lever_a_gate.one_line: The scheduled session-fetch is age-gated, not daily, which is why 09-16 -> 09-24 shows an 8-day gap under a cron(30 7 * * ? *) schedule and why 09-24..09-27 then fired four days running.
lever_a_gate.mechanism: Lever A in cot-bd-session-trigger SKIPS the session-fetch entirely when the stored .bd.identity probes POSITIVE-live AND captured_at is younger than MAX_SESSION_AGE_DAYS (unset in env -> default 7). Measured now via the Lambda's own read-only mode=session-check: session_live true, captured_at 2026-09-27T18:42:27.162Z. At 09-28 07:30 ET the capture is ~0.53d old, so the scheduled run dispatches opal-cot-bronze-run directly and opal-cot-bd-session-fetch does NOT run. The next expected session-fetch is when the capture passes 7 days (~2026-10-04 07:30 ET) or the probe goes negative sooner.
lever_a_gate.why_the_four_days_fired_daily: 09-24 was 8 days after the 09-16 capture, so the age bound was exceeded and the mint leg fired. A failed mint leaves the live cookie untouched by design, so the capture stayed over-age and the mint re-fired on 09-25, 09-26 and 09-27. That explains the FIRING pattern; it does not name the proximate login failure.
lever_a_gate.instrument: aws lambda invoke --function-name cot-bd-session-trigger --payload '{"mode":"session-check"}' (the Lambda's own read-only probe -- no secret value read), plus the unpacked function source _session_is_positive_live / _handle_session_refresh.
